learning_objective: 🎯 Step inside the Parliament! Understand how laws are made, how the government is held accountable, and the roles of the Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha.

main_concepts.concept_title: 🏛️ Why do we need a Parliament?
main_concepts.simple_explanation: It is not just for making laws. It is the center of all democratic political process. It ensures representation, debate, holds the executive accountable, and controls the nation's finances.

India has a bicameral (two-house) Parliament: The Lok Sabha (House of the People) and the Rajya Sabha (Council of States). Bicameralism ensures double-check on hasty laws and gives representation to states.

Lok Sabha represents the people directly and has more power, especially over Money Bills and bringing down the government. Rajya Sabha represents the states and is a permanent body (cannot be fully dissolved).

main_concepts.concept_title: 📜 How does a Bill become a Law?
main_concepts.simple_explanation: A bill undergoes three readings in one house, gets passed, goes to the other house for the same process, and finally goes to the President for assent. If both houses clash, a joint session may be called (except for Money Bills).
Parliament controls the government through mechanisms like Question Hour, Zero Hour, debates, approval of budgets, and the ultimate weapon: the No-Confidence Motion.

fun_activity.title: 📜 Pass the Bill!
fun_activity.instructions: Draft a 'Homework Ban Bill'. Present it to your friends (Lok Sabha). Let them debate it. If they pass it, take it to your parents (Rajya Sabha). See if it survives the whole process or gets vetoed!

exam_tips: 📌 Clearly outline the special powers of the Lok Sabha (Money bills, no-confidence motion) and the special powers of the Rajya Sabha (state list laws).
📌 Understand the difference between an Ordinary Bill, a Money Bill, and a Constitutional Amendment Bill.
📌 Know the purpose of Parliamentary Committees (they do the detailed, technical work outside the noisy house).
quick_recap: ⭐ The Rajya Sabha is a permanent house; one-third of its members retire every two years.
⭐ A Money Bill can only be introduced in the Lok Sabha.
⭐ Defection is when a member leaves the party whose symbol they used to get elected.
